nodes.label: Choreography boot gating (director:ready -> preloader:out -> LandingSequence)
nodes.rationale: Preloader and choreography must never bypass this gating order; preloader event names are imported from choreography config rather than hardcoded to avoid drift.

nodes.label: Reduced-motion graceful degradation
nodes.rationale: Motion must preserve intent under prefers-reduced-motion (shorten/simplify/crossfade) rather than disabling all motion, so meaning is not conveyed by motion alone.

nodes.label: LCP asset + font preload strategy
nodes.rationale: Preloading the true LCP asset and first hero font, plus deferring choreography JS, targets FCP/LCP on first visit without blocking the parser.

nodes.label: AIX context hygiene principle
nodes.rationale: Generated or stale files actively harm Copilot/AI suggestion accuracy; deletion improves AIX faster than adding rules.

nodes.label: Link, don't fork (AI docs portability)
nodes.rationale: Copying AIX checklists/evaluation prompts between repos causes drift; prefer pointers from an external scaffold into this repo's AI docs.

nodes.label: Eleventy service layer pattern
nodes.rationale: Business logic is encapsulated in reusable/testable service classes (NavigationBuilder, TailwindLogger) separated from 11ty collection registration, isolating errors and improving maintainability.

nodes.label: Collection initialization dependency order (Sanity before Navigation)
nodes.rationale: 11ty processes collections synchronously during build; navigation collections depend on Sanity project data already being present, so Sanity collections must register first.
nodes.norm_label: collection initialization dependency order (sanity before navigation)

nodes.label: Atomic Design Pattern (atoms→molecules→organisms→templates)
nodes.rationale: Blockframes uses atomic design (atoms→molecules→organisms→templates) so wireframe SVG mockups can be composed and recolored consistently, mirroring frontend component structure.

nodes.norm_label: effects package (text, transitions, gel, halftone, parallax)

nodes.label: prefers-reduced-motion accessibility pattern
nodes.rationale: All effects check reducedMotionHandler.isReducedMotion() and substitute an instant final gsap.set() state instead of animating, so motion-sensitive users get equivalent end states without vestibular triggers.

nodes.label: GSAP local-copy detection for ScrollSmoother compatibility
nodes.rationale: The preloader checks whether GSAP is already available locally/vendored before the main GSAP + plugin bundle loads at the end of the page, so it can cooperate with ScrollSmoother if present instead of double-loading or conflicting.
nodes.norm_label: gsap local-copy detection for scrollsmoother compatibility

nodes.label: Frontend build order (clean→design→css→js→ 11ty)
nodes.rationale: build:design must run before build:css because Tailwind compiles against Figma-generated design tokens (styles/colors.css, fontFamilies.css); build:11ty runs last because it fetches Sanity data and consumes all prepared CSS/JS assets.

attributes.role: Page narrative flow — choreographs the complete landing page animation sequence by listening to AnimationBus events and coordinating section transitions
attributes.rationale: Owns no DOM and no ScrollTrigger — it listens on AnimationBus and cues section lifecycle methods in order, so it never reaches into an organism's internals beyond its public play* methods.

nodes.label: Reduced-motion variant-swap contract (Awards)
nodes.rationale: The reduced motion profile swaps the entire award-motion variant to reduced.js so the full-motion slide.js is never built and needs no reduced branch of its own — reduced motion is handled at the variant-selection layer, not inline.

nodes.label: Use `from` not `to` for fluid-dimension content reveals
nodes.rationale: Content uses GSAP `from` so it captures each child's laid-out position as the end state and re-reads it on refresh, avoiding a computed destination and the pin-measurement feedback loop that previously made `view` jitter when children were the trigger element.
nodes.norm_label: use `from` not `to` for fluid-dimension content reveals

nodes.label: Bio fade variant currently inert (commented out)
nodes.rationale: Every factory body is commented out but timelines are still built and tagged with TIMELINE_IDS so AbstractSection can bind lifecycle callbacks and the phase still completes, just playing nothing; distinct from bio reduced.js which is intentionally empty by design rather than by accident.
nodes.norm_label: bio fade variant currently inert (commented out)

nodes.label: Bio reduced variant hides gel as correct rest state
nodes.rationale: gel_bio exists only as a motion device; without the wipe there is nothing for it to express, and left visible it would sit as an opaque sheet over the fixed background video — so init sets autoAlpha:0 as the correct rest state, not merely the absence of animation.
nodes.norm_label: bio reduced variant hides gel as correct rest state

nodes.label: Cache/revert SplitText instance across matchMedia rebuilds
nodes.rationale: _buildTimeline() re-runs intro() on every matchMedia breakpoint crossing against the same already-split DOM; without caching + revert()-ing the prior SplitText instance first, a rebuild would nest split markup inside itself and corrupt both intro chars and outro line targets.
nodes.norm_label: cache/revert splittext instance across matchmedia rebuilds

nodes.label: bioRectAsViewportPercent conversion pattern
nodes.rationale: gel_bio is absolute inset-0 inside the fixed inset-0 #sizzle-background container, so its percentages resolve against the viewport, not the bio section; bioRectAsViewportPercent converts the bio section's getBoundingClientRect() into viewport percentages so the sweep doesn't blanket the fixed background video.

nodes.label: Per-view WeakMap SplitText state tracking
nodes.rationale: Splits are tracked per-view in a module-level WeakMap so revertSplit runs first on rebuild, reverting the prior split rather than nesting wrappers; WeakMap keying means a discarded view is garbage-collected without manual cleanup.

nodes.label: Non-literal dynamic import to keep blockframes package out of bundle
nodes.rationale: The js/displays/blockframes package is dynamic-imported with a non-literal specifier so esbuild leaves it out of the choreography bundle, because the package's https CDN imports can't be bundled.
nodes.norm_label: non-literal dynamic import to keep blockframes package out of bundle

nodes.label: Progressive enhancement (no-JS fallback) pattern
nodes.rationale: ContactForm and Lightbox both accept that without JavaScript the trigger/form renders but does not activate — an accepted tradeoff rather than server-rendered fallback behavior.

attributes.rationale: Item 3 now routes to the vault-root goals/ folder — a sibling of the dataink.io/ directory — under Obsidian's Project Manager plugin, because goals migrated out of the repo. Task frontmatter is the source of truth and status: "in-progress" marks active work.

attributes.fast_path: single-file edit, template lookup, quick question — portfolio-frontend.md + copilot-instructions.md only
attributes.full_path: implementation, choreography, architecture, multi-file — all four orientation docs
attributes.rationale: Spend reads in cost order so trivial tasks do not pay the full orientation cost.

attributes.location: vault-root goals/ (../../goals/), a sibling of the dataink.io/ directory — NOT inside this repo
attributes.source_of_truth: task frontmatter; a project note's taskIds and ## Tasks checklist are plugin-generated and drift
attributes.removed_paths: frontend/context/current-goals.md and frontend/context/goals/ do not exist — removed when goals migrated to the vault root; do not recreate
attributes.rationale: Goals moved to Obsidian's Project Manager plugin at the vault root so a single dashboard spans all projects; never fork or restate goals into this repo — link to them. type: subtask entries are deliberately absent from the top-level checklist.

attributes.rules: page-level work starts at views/pages/<name>/<name>.njk; never infer source behavior from _site/ (but do read rendered _site/<page>.html to verify output); never hand-edit styles/colors.css or styles/typography/fontFamilies.css; never call Tailwind CLI directly; never bypass choreography lifecycle gating; never introduce new global singletons; CSS import order in styles/main.css is fonts → Tailwind → base → theme → components; templates live in views/, not njk/
attributes.rationale: The documented system is not the page — confirm real above-the-fold composition and the true LCP element from the template before forming a hypothesis. Generated files (colors.css, fontFamilies.css) are overwritten by build:design, so hand edits are lost.

attributes.commands: npm start (Tailwind watch + 11ty serve), npm run build, npm run quick (skips Figma sync), npm run build:design (Figma tokens → CSS), npm run validate, npm run scaffold:component
attributes.rationale: build:design syncs Figma tokens into CSS and must run before build:css, otherwise the CSS build consumes stale token output.

attributes.agents: choreographer (motion/GSAP/ScrollTrigger/reduced-motion), implementer (code changes, components, Sanity wiring), mechanic (build failures, 11ty config, tooling), reviewer (pre-merge, diff, contract compliance), planner (sequence multi-step work), taskmaster (embed TODOs for GitHub Issues workflow)

attributes.skills: gsap-core, gsap-timeline (LandingSequence), gsap-scrolltrigger, gsap-plugins, gsap-performance, gsap-utils; gsap-react and gsap-frameworks not used in this project
attributes.rationale: Skills are installed globally at ~/.claude/skills/; load only what the task needs rather than all by default. The choreographer agent selects the right skill automatically.

attributes.tiers: opus for choreography/motion implementation and page-level planning; sonnet for template/component implementation and Sanity wiring; haiku for copy tweaks, sidecar docs, formatting
attributes.rationale: Motion timing and LCP judgment need the strongest model; mechanical doc/format work does not.
Always emit/listen via AnimationBus — never call sections directly, so cross-section coordination stays event-driven.

attributes.sequence: DOMContentLoaded (idle-deferred) → AnimationDirector constructs bus, ScrollEffectsCoordinator, CardManager, SECTION_REGISTRY, managers, LandingSequence → window director:ready → Preloader exit animation → window preloader:out
attributes.rationale: Never bypass. LandingSequence.start() only stages the video's landing (hidden resting) state at preloader:out; playing the video intro there would race the header.

attributes.chain: HomeHeaderManager._arm → HOME_HERO_HOLD.delay (gsap.delayedCall) → HomeHeaderManager._runTransition (deconstruct) → home:outro:complete → LandingSequence._startVideoIntro (video.playIntro, awaits _ensureVideoReady) → video:intro:complete → LandingSequence._armBioIntro (BIO_INTRO_HOLD.delay) → await bio.playLanding (BIO_GEL_ENTRANCE) → landing timeline onComplete → bio.playIntro → bio:intro:complete → HomeHeaderManager._playMenuIn → home:intro:complete
attributes.rationale: The header opens the landing and closes it: hero exit is the page's first statement, the video reveal answers it, Bio follows a beat later, and the menu rail arrives last once Bio has had its say.

Load-bearing: the menu rail's build waits for bio:intro:complete (HomeHeaderManager._playMenuIn), so cueing Bio's chain off the rail's intro would deadlock — the rail waiting on Bio, Bio waiting on the rail. The hero exiting is the earlier, unblocked cue. Anything later added to this chain must respect that cycle.

nodes.label: Every Link Is an Event, Not a Call

attributes.rationale: Cross-section coordination goes through AnimationBus with EVENTS constants; LandingSequence never reaches into an organism's internals beyond its public play* methods, keeping sections decoupled and independently testable.

nodes.norm_label: every link is an event, not a call

nodes.label: Reduced Motion Zeroes Holds Rather Than Skipping Links

attributes.rationale: A gated profile still emits …:intro:complete (AbstractSection jumps the intro to progress(1)), so the chain completes without motion instead of stalling. Holds go to zero and timelines jump to progress 1 — events still emit and the chain stays intact.

nodes.norm_label: reduced motion zeroes holds rather than skipping links

attributes.rationale: gsap.delayedCall is ticker-synced, pausable, and killable in destroy(); setTimeout is none of those and would leak past teardown.

Bio's ScrollTrigger still fires enter/exit/onEnterBack/onLeaveBack for side effects and logging, but the reveal is owned by the landing chain — the reveal is disengaged from scroll so narrative pacing, not scroll position, drives it.

nodes.label: Gel Entrance Gates the Bio Intro

attributes.rationale: bio.playLanding() is awaited, not fired-and-forgotten — the heading band has to land before the SplitText reveal starts over it. The promise resolves via AbstractSection's PromiseResolverQueue and resolves immediately under a gated profile so the await can never stall the chain.

nodes.norm_label: gel entrance gates the bio intro

attributes.rationale: A prior note flagged BackgroundVideo.playIntro()'s comment for claiming LandingSequence waits on video:intro:complete to trigger hero.playLanding(). That comment no longer exists — playIntro() now carries only a reduced-motion note, and hero.playLanding appears nowhere in organisms/background/ or templates/landing/. The chain has always triggered bio.playIntro(); the mermaid diagram (VIC → BEAT → GEL → BIO) is the accurate account.
These sections are driven by their own ScrollTriggers rather than the serial landing chain, so they are out of band from LandingSequence's narrative pacing.
